title: Haven Analytics — inference economics casefile
content:
Summary:
Haven Analytics (enterprise analytics product, ~12M monthly active users) asked for a quick before/after economics snapshot to understand potential savings from applying Redwood Optimize recommendations to their primary inference workload (customer-facing summarization + Q&A). This doc collates baseline telemetry, conservative Redwood recommendations, and an estimated savings runway with rollout/validation advice.

Customer context and constraints:
- Product: query -> long-context summarization (avg user prompt 120 tokens, system/context 1800 tokens across doc sections) + follow-up QA (avg 80 tokens).
- SLA: 95th percentile latency target < 450ms for primary interactive route; offline batch summarization tolerant of up to 2s p95.
- Privacy: runs on Dedicated (reserved capacity) in us-west with customer-managed VPC. No model weights may leave tenant.
- Quality bar: human-evaluated ROUGE/QA pass rate must not degrade by >2 pts on our critical eval set.

Baseline (current setup reported by Haven infra team):
- Model: custom fine-tuned 13B transformer (float16), served on a2-high-gpu equivalent (A100-80GB cluster).
- Serving config: concurrency per GPU 12, dynamic batching disabled, KV cache disabled between requests, no quantization.
- Average request: prompt tokens 1,920 (context + prompt), completion tokens 256.
- Avg tokens per request = 2,176.
- Monthly request volume: 930k requests (peak daily QPS ~120).
- Measured p50/p95 latency: 160ms / 620ms (current infra shows p95 misses SLA).
- Direct infra cost (estimated from customer billing): $82,600 / month (GPU-only cost basis).
- Upstream software/ops overhead (model versioning, storage, network): additional $12,100 / month.
- Total baseline monthly: $94,700.

Baseline per-unit math (for internal sanity checks):
- Total monthly tokens = 930k * 2,176 = ~2.02B tokens.
- Effective cost per 1M tokens (baseline) = $94,700 / 2,020 ≈ $46.86 per 1M tokens.

Redwood Optimize conservative recommendation set (targeting minimal quality risk):
1) 4-bit quantized variant of same model (q4_0) with Redwood-verified FP16-to-Q4 conversion and calibration (expected latency ~ -18% on token generation).
2) Enable prefix KV caching for repeated document context chunks (Haven has many repeated templates). Expect cache hit rate 22% initially, rising to 35% with TTL tuning.
3) Dynamic batching with 80ms batching window during peak to increase GPU utilization without exceeding latency SLO (adaptive per-route).
4) Response length cap and smart truncation/summary-first heuristic: reduce average completion tokens from 256 to 200 via heuristic/reranking (lossy for long tails only).
5) Recommend switching cold/low-complexity queries to a distilled 7B quantized variant for eligibility (policy-based routing: cost-tier fallback).

Estimated technical impacts (conservative assumptions):
- Quantization q4 -> token compute cost reduction: 42% (expected).
- Caching: reduce repeated-token decoding by 22% initially (applies to prefix tokens only; we conservatively translate to 11% total token reduction).
- Batching: efficiency gain ~12% in throughput for GPU pools (reduces required reserved capacity).
- Completion cap: 22% reduction on completion token volume.
- Routing to 7B for eligible queries: 16% of requests (low-complexity) switched, 60% per-token compute reduction for those requests.

Conservative combined effect (composition, conservative overlaps accounted):
- Net token-equivalent compute reduction estimated at ~55% overall.
- Expected p95 latency change: p95 improves from 620ms -> ~410ms (meets SLA) due to quantization + batching; p50 improves slightly.

Before / After (monthly cost projection, conservative):
- Baseline monthly total: $94,700 (as above).
- After applying Redwood Optimize config (projected):
  - Reduced GPU hours (fewer required instances) and per-token cost -> estimated infra + ops $42,300 / month.
  - Additional one-time migration/validation engineering (non-recurring): $24,000 (3 people * 2 weeks effort + infra for calibration).
  - Total monthly (steady-state): $42,300.
- Projected monthly savings: $94,700 - $42,300 = $52,400 (≈55% savings).
- 12-month run-rate savings (steady-state) ≈ $628,800 excluding migration cost.

Quality and risk notes (areas for close monitoring):
- Quantization risks: edge-case numeric instability on some generation heuristics — mitigated by fallback to FP16 for flagged prompts and running an automated eval harness across 2k prompts during canary.
- Routing correctness: must ensure policy does not route high-complexity legal/financial queries to distilled 7B. Use existing intent classifier (JIRA-ML-953) to gate.
- Cache staleness: TTL misconfiguration could return stale context; recommend conservative initial TTL=30m and metrics on cache hit/miss patterns.

Validation plan and rollout steps (recommended):
- Phase 0 (sandbox): run q4 and 7B variants in isolated Dedicated pool with production shadow traffic for 2 weeks. Collect token-level latency, quality diffs, and cache hit rates. (Owner: ENG-optimize)
- Phase 1 (canary 10%): route 10% live traffic to q4 + caching + batching config; keep FP16 fallback on errors or quality regression >2 pts (24/7 monitoring). Run human eval on 500 samples daily. (Owner: Solutions Eng)
- Phase 2 (canary 50%): expand to 50% after 7 days of stable metrics; enable routing to 7B for policy-eligible queries. (Owner: Product/Optimize)
- Phase 3 (full): complete cutover, retire some baseline capacity. Reconcile billing and update runbook. (Owner: SRE)

KPIs to track during rollout:
- p95 latency (target <450ms).
- Mean tokens generated per request.
- Cache hit rate and effective token reduction.
- Aggregate monthly GPU-hours and per-month bill.
- Quality delta on eval set (ROUGE / exact-match / human-pass).
- Error/fallback rate to FP16 or baseline model.

Open questions for Haven + next actions (TODOs):
- Confirm acceptance criteria for quality (exact metric and threshold for rollback).
- Provide sample of 5k recent production prompts for offline calibration run (privacy filtered).
- Approve Dedicated pool size reduction schedule (ops to suggest exact capacity steps).
- Budget sign-off for one-time migration engineering ($24k).

Appendix: rough token math and sensitivity table (showing sensitivity to caching hit rate and percent routed to 7B):
- Sensitivity knobs (conservative baseline):
  - If cache hit rate stays at 10% instead of 22% -> projected savings drop to ~45% ($42k/mo savings).
  - If routing to 7B can only be 8% of traffic -> savings drop to ~49%.
  - If quantization underperforms (only 30% compute reduction) -> savings drop to ~38% (recommend holdback).

Notes & links:
- Detailed per-route spreadsheet (runs + simulation) here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HavenOptimizeModelRunMock
- Related tickets: JIRA-OPT-412 (optimize plan), JIRA-ML-953 (intent classifier gating).
- Slack thread: #optimize-haven (see linked_artifacts).

Author: Priya Natarajan (product-optimize) — draft for review. Comments welcome from Marco, Leah, Owen.

Checklist before sending to customer:
- [ ] run 5k-sample offline q4 calibration and store results in sheet above
- [ ] produce 2-page executive one-pager summarizing savings and migration timeline
- [ ] create playbook runbook for rollback/fallback
- [ ] schedule 30-min customer review with Haven infra + product next week

End of casefile.
